problem_statement: ByteGrad/portfolio-website is a runnable Next.js 13 App Router + Tailwind developer portfolio for the persona Ricardo, a full-stack developer. The site is a single scrolling page (Intro, About, My projects, Skills, My experience, Contact) with a fixed pill navbar and a footer, and a light/dark theme toggle. Its 'My projects' section already tells Ricardo's story through his shipped work (CorpComment, rmtDev, Word Analytics). Design and ship the portfolio's OWN 'Selected work' project browser: a section that lists six grounded project cards (CorpComment, rmtDev, Word Analytics, Ledger Sync, Palette API, Focus Timer), each tagged with a track, above a row of track tabs (All / Frontend / Full-stack / Backend) derived from the projects' own discipline metadata. Clicking a track tab must actually re-render the card grid to the matching projects and update a genuine result count, for example 'Showing all 6 projects' becomes 'Showing 3 of 6 · Frontend' when the Frontend tab is selected. The browser is a shared project navigator that stays continuous across the portfolio: its track-tab row and count readout appear on the home page and on two dedicated work routes (/work and /stack), and the full card grid renders on the home page where the projects live. Keep the existing Ricardo identity intact (the hero, About, My projects, Skills, My experience and Contact sections, the pill navbar and footer, and the rounded gray card + pill-tag visual language), keep the browser's track row and card grid within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, keep the active track tab clearly legible, and emit no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real 'Selected work' project browser sits on the home page with track tabs (All / Frontend / Full-stack / Backend) built from the projects' discipline metadata; clicking a track tab re-renders the project cards to the matching track.
The browser shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active track (e.g. 'Showing all 6 projects' becomes 'Showing 3 of 6 · Frontend' when the Frontend tab is selected).

The project browser (its track-tab row and count readout) is shared across the portfolio and appears on the home page, the /work route AND the /stack route (cross-route continuity); the full card grid renders on the home page.

The track-tab row and the filtered card grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow and lay out cleanly (tabs wrap or shrink, cards wrap into columns rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The browser adopts the portfolio's own rounded gray card + pill-tag language and dark-mode variants, and the active track tab is clearly legible (not dark-on-dark) — an on-brand project browser, not an off-palette or broken control.

The existing Ricardo persona stays intact: the Intro hero, About, My projects, Skills, My experience and Contact sections, the pill navbar and footer all continue to render alongside the new browser, and all captured states emit no runtime console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the portfolio's visual language: the rounded gray panels, the pill-style tags, the section heading treatment, the fixed pill navbar and footer, and the light/dark theme variants; the browser and its cards must adopt this same identity.
Build the track tabs from the projects' own discipline metadata, and render the shared browser so a single component covers the home, /work, and /stack routes rather than duplicating markup per page.

The track-tab row must wrap or shrink and stay within the mobile viewport at 390px, and the filtered card grid must reflow into columns on narrow screens — do not pin the tabs to a fixed desktop width or force the cards into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone.

The result count and the visible card set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected track; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave it stale when a tab is clicked.
Do not remove any existing home-page section, and do not introduce remote images, generated media, new packages or backend dependencies; keep the site a single-persona developer portfolio.
Keep the whole page responsive and uncluttered on desktop, tablet and at 390px mobile with no horizontal overflow and no runtime console or network errors.
state_constraints: desktop_home and tablet_home verify the existing Ricardo hero, About, My projects, Skills, My experience and Contact sections remain intact and that the 'Selected work' browser renders with its track tabs.
mobile_home captures the home at 390px where the whole page must stay within the viewport.
desktop_work scrolls the 'Selected work' browser into view and captures the track-tab row (All active), the result count ('Showing all 6 projects'), and the six project cards laid out cleanly.

mobile_work scrolls the browser into view at 390px and captures the track row and card grid reflowed within the viewport - this is where a fixed-width non-wrapping track forces the page to scroll sideways.
desktop_filter_frontend captures the browser after clicking the 'Frontend' track tab: the grid re-filters to the three Frontend projects and the count updates to 'Showing 3 of 6 · Frontend'.
desktop_route_work and desktop_route_stack capture the /work and /stack routes, where the shared project browser (its track-tab row and count) must also be present (cross-route continuity).

change_completion: The 'Selected work' section has a working track-filter control (All / Frontend / Full-stack / Backend) on home.
Clicking a track tab re-renders the project cards to that track and updates the result count to reflect it.
The Ricardo persona (hero, About, My projects, Skills, My experience, Contact, navbar, footer) remains intact alongside the browser.
design_consistency: The browser and cards adopt the portfolio's rounded gray card + pill-tag language and dark-mode variants, with a legible active tab.
The shared browser rides home, /work, and /stack continuously (track-tab row + count readout).
The card and typography language is preserved across the browser and the existing sections.
regression: No home-page section is removed and the Ricardo hero, My projects and Contact still render their content.
The browser appears on the /work and /stack routes, not only on home, confirming cross-route continuity.
The repair does not rely on an overflow-x:hidden hack over a still-oversized fixed-width row.
responsive: 390px mobile has no horizontal overflow; the track-tab row wraps/shrinks and stays within the viewport.
The filtered card grid reflows into columns on mobile without spilling, overlapping, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 13 App Router portfolio task at L4 on ByteGrad/portfolio-website, capability=Consistency, scope=cross_page. The graded change designs the portfolio's OWN 'Selected work' project browser: a track-tab control (All / Frontend / Full-stack / Backend) built from the project cards' discipline metadata that actually re-renders the cards and updates a real result count, shared across the home, /work, and /stack routes. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile browser (the track-tab row must wrap, not pin to a fixed/narrow desktop width); visual_regression on the browser component crops at desktop_work + mobile_work + desktop_filter_frontend (on-brand rounded gray card grid with a legible active tab, not a broken overlapping shingled grid with an illegible dark-on-dark tab); cross-route dom_assertions that the browser tab row (pwork__title 'Selected work') rides /work and /stack as well as home; and interaction_assertions that clicking the Frontend tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to 'Showing 3 of 6 · Frontend' (a snapshotted grid + count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is a plausible v0 layout defect (track row pinned to a fixed 620px non-wrapping width, present on home only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-route but passes interaction; the known-bad 'smart wrong' browser keeps a narrow non-wrapping off-layout track row, breaks the filtered card grid into a single overflowing overlapping row with a dark-on-dark active tab, is home-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale, failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): next/font/google Inter replaced with a local font stack; the Resend email send in actions/sendEmail.ts stubbed offline; the remote Unsplash next/image avatar replaced with a local public/avatar.png; two work routes (/work, /stack) added so the cross-route continuity gate has real secondary routes; and the react-vertical-timeline mobile overflow in the Experience section clipped with a scoped overflow-x:clip (a measurement-enabling clip on an unrelated section, not a fix of the graded browser). The project images corpcomment.png, rmtdev.png and wordanalytics.png are the local design assets reused as-is.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: ByteGrad/portfolio-website is a runnable Next.js 13 App Router developer portfolio with a real 'My projects' section rendered from a shared data module (lib/data.ts) and a rounded gray card + pill-tag design system; a design_continuity task adds the project grid's OWN track-filter browser that re-renders the cards and updates a result count, shared across the home, /work, and /stack routes — exercising cross-route continuity, responsive layout, visual fidelity, and interaction wiring on one repo-native surface (the project browser).
